plain_english_policy: This bill creates a new commission called 'United We Ride' inside the Department of Senior Services in Alabama. Its main goal is to improve transportation access for people with disabilities, seniors, and low-income individuals by coordinating efforts across different government agencies.
policy_direction_if_enacted: Enactment would establish a formal structure (the United We Ride Commission) comprising representatives from various state departments (Health, Education, Medicaid, Human Resources, Mental Health, Rehabilitation, Transportation, etc.) to oversee transportation coordination. The commission's duties include developing educational plans for better local access, reducing duplicate or restrictive laws regarding human service transportation, identifying cost-effective strategies across federal/state/local levels, and holding regular meetings with the public. It would also require all cabinet-level agencies to cooperate fully with this new body.
sponsorship_supports_position: The sponsors (Representatives McCampbell and Harper) affirmatively advanced the creation of a commission to coordinate transportation services for vulnerable populations.
evidence_quotes: This bill would establish, within the Department of Senior Services, the United We Ride Commission. This bill would provide for membership, terms of office, and duties; and would provide for an annual report to the Governor.

(1) To develop an educational plan for coordinated human service transportation intended to result in enhanced customer access, at the local level, for individuals with disabilities, older adults, and individuals with lower income.
(2) To help reduce or eliminate restrictive and duplicative laws, regulations, and programs related to human service transportation.
